title: Evel Knievel Part II
summary: Part two of the Evel Knievel story. After his Caesar's Palace crash, Knievel pushes for a Grand Canyon jump, which the Interior Department refuses. He instead targets the Snake River Canyon near Twin Falls, Idaho, in September 1974. A steam-powered rocket built by engineer Robert Truax is used; the parachute deploys early, and Knievel drifts down to land near the river. Speculation is raised that he pulled the chute deliberately. The episode then covers his later jumps (Wembley Stadium crash and broken back, King's Island, Cedar Point-area ABC broadcasts), his retirements, the planned shark jump and the cameraman injury, his record number of broken bones, his drinking and drug rumors, Shelly Saltman's tell-all book, the baseball bat attack that led to six months in prison, the loss of licensing income, the 1977 film Viva Knievel, his later life, illness, death, burial in Butte in 2007, and his honor at the X Games. The episode closes with listener mail from a PhD student about the chaos theory episode.

segments.title: Intro and recap of Caesar's Palace crash
segments.summary: Hosts introduce part two of the Evel Knievel story and recap his Caesar's Palace jump crash, noting his coma and his lifestyle.

segments.title: Grand Canyon jump ambitions and Idaho plan
segments.summary: After the Caesar's Palace crash, Knievel pushes for a Grand Canyon jump, but the Interior Department denies airspace. He instead finds a site over the Snake River Canyon near Twin Falls, Idaho, which is privately owned.

segments.title: Rocket design and promotion
segments.summary: Knievel's team, with promoter Bob Arum, plans closed-circuit TV coverage. An X-1 rocket motorcycle test runs into the river, so the team turns to a steam rocket designed by Robert Truax, whose son Eddie Braun later attempts a jump to vindicate his father.

segments.title: Party crowd and the Snake River jump
segments.summary: Thousands of biker and hippie visitors turn Twin Falls into a three-day party, with fears of a crowd crush at the canyon edge. Knievel says goodbye to his family and launches in the steam rocket. The parachute deploys early and he drifts down, landing near the river.

segments.title: Speculation about the parachute
segments.summary: Hosts discuss speculation that Knievel pulled the parachute deliberately, the engineer's surprise at being publicly blamed, and the money from the jump.

segments.title: Wide World of Sports jumps and merchandising
segments.summary: Knievel's fame grows through Wide World of Sports, the Stunt Cycle toy, Atari game, action figures, and endorsements. Hosts compare the seventies daredevil star to later celebrities.

segments.title: Wembley crash, King's Island jump, and retirements
segments.summary: Knievel crashes at Wembley Stadium in London, breaking his back but walking out. He later jumps buses at King's Island in Ohio successfully, and repeatedly announces retirements before returning.

segments.title: Shark jump plan and cameraman injury
segments.summary: Knievel plans to jump a tank of sharks inspired by Jaws, but a rehearsal crash seriously injures a cameraman who loses an eye. The jump is called off, and the footage is held for about twenty years.

segments.title: Injuries, broken bones record, and drinking
segments.summary: Hosts list Knievel's injuries, including a record number of broken bones, and discuss rumors of drug and alcohol use and his daily drinking.

segments.title: Saltman book, baseball bat attack, and prison
segments.summary: Shelly Saltman's tell-all book exposes Knievel's behavior. Knievel attacks Saltman with a baseball bat and serves six months in prison, losing licensing income. The Human Fly fills the daredevil gap.

segments.title: Viva Knievel, later life, death, and legacy
segments.summary: Knievel makes the 1977 film Viva Knievel with Gene Kelly and Lauren Hutton. He later lives with partner Krystal Kennedy, dies of lung disease, is buried in Butte in 2007, and is honored at the X Games.

segments.title: Listener mail: differential equations
segments.summary: A listener who is a PhD student in mechanical engineering comments on the chaos theory episode and the Isaac Newton episode.

segments.title: Outro
segments.summary: Hosts give contact details and sign off.
